question.text: The variation of velocity with time for a body executing one-dimensional motion is depicted in the given diagram. The body starts from an initial position of s = −10 m at t = 0 s. Draw the corresponding acceleration-time (a-t) and displacement-time (s-t) graphs for the entire interval from t = 0 s to t = 10 s.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Plot the acceleration-time (a-t) graph for the interval t = 0 s to t = 10 s.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Plot the position-time (s-t) graph for the interval t = 0 s to t = 10 s.

conditions: at t = 0 s, position s = −10 m
from t = 0 s to t = 2 s, velocity increases linearly from 0 m/s to 10 m/s
from t = 2 s to t = 4 s, velocity remains constant at 10 m/s
from t = 4 s to t = 8 s, velocity decreases linearly from 10 m/s to −10 m/s (crossing 0 m/s at t = 6 s)
from t = 8 s to t = 10 s, velocity increases linearly from −10 m/s to 0 m/s

figure.description: A velocity versus time (v-t) graph displaying piecewise linear segments from t = 0 s to t = 10 s. The velocity starts at (0 s, 0 m/s), increases linearly to (2 s, 10 m/s), remains flat at 10 m/s until (4 s, 10 m/s), drops linearly through (6 s, 0 m/s) to reach a minimum of −10 m/s at (8 s, −10 m/s), and finally rises linearly to end at (10 s, 0 m/s).

solution.approach: Read the slope of each straight segment of the v-t graph for acceleration, and add the signed area under v-t to the initial position for the s-t graph.

steps.text: Find acceleration on each segment as the slope of the v-t line; the acceleration graph is a step function.
Start the position at s = −10 m at t = 0 and add the area under v-t up to each breakpoint.
Between breakpoints, the s-t graph is a parabola while v is changing, and a straight line while v is constant.
steps.equation: s(t) = −10 + 2.5t² for 0≤t≤2 s; s(t) = 10t − 20 for 2≤t≤4 s; curved between 4 and 8 s with a peak s = 30 m at t = 6 s (where v = 0); curved between 8 and 10 s
steps.why_this_step: The s-t curve bends wherever v itself is changing, and is straight only while v is constant.

final_answer.value: a-t graph: a = 5 m/s² from t = 0–2 s, a = 0 from t = 2–4 s, a = −5 m/s² from t = 4–8 s, a = 5 m/s² from t = 8–10 s (a step graph). s-t graph passes through (0,−10), (2,0), (4,20), (6,30) [peak, since v = 0 here], (8,20), (10,10) m — a rising parabola from t = 0–2 s, a straight rising line from t = 2–4 s, and parabolic curves from t = 4–8 s and t = 8–10 s.

common_mistakes.text: Treating the s-t graph as straight lines between every pair of breakpoints instead of a curve wherever the velocity is itself changing.
Missing that acceleration is zero during the constant-velocity segment from t = 2 s to t = 4 s, and drawing a nonzero acceleration there instead.

concept_tags: s-t graph from area under v-t
